04 / 21 · Foundation

Graph structure

Entities represent resources, services or other domain objects. Directed relationships connect them. Both carry an ID, a type and typed properties.

Contract illustration
Master graph
◉ Active+ Added− RemovedΔ Changed× Rejected
The rule
What the contract requires
A relationship has entity endpoints and its own projection-specific ID. Different relationship types can connect the same pair.
The boundary
Scope and constraints
Removing a node may leave an unresolved endpoint. Missing and not-yet-examined are distinct read outcomes.
Example · C#
Put data on an edge
Full source ↗
An observed call has an identity, endpoints, a type and a health property.
UsageExamples.cs
public static RelationshipState ObservedCall(
    RelationshipId edge, EntityId api, EntityId database) =>
    new(edge, api, database, new TypeId("Calls"),
        [new(new PropertyId("health"), new TextValue("degraded"))]);
// The output ontology must declare Calls and its text-valued health property.
// The relationship's identity belongs to its projection, not its current type.
Compile-checked caller example. Execution requires implementations of the injected interfaces.
